title: Scoped UIA subtree observation (bounded observation below an Orcel-issued element)
objective: Make the controls of Chromium- and Electron-rendered windows observable, and so targetable by the existing approval-gated UIA actions, without widening any per-call bound. Today uia.tree observe stops at depth 8, which ends exactly at Chromium's web Document (BM-02 Tier C evidence, run 40784710382: 11 nodes, deepest 8, truncated, only the Document actionable). SG-000128 adds an optional scoped root: uia.tree observe may name an element orceld itself issued for the same window in its current tree generation, and returns the bounded subtree below it under exactly today's caps, redaction and protected-surface rules. Preparation packet: docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/UIA_SUBTREE_OBSERVATION.md (PR #517).

include: Activate the SG-000128 contract only. Every slice below needs its own exact-head qualified implementation PR with a fresh-context security judge.

Slice 1, kernel and provider: orcel-policy (SG-000027) admits two optional uia.tree observe arguments, root_element_id and expected_tree_generation, both or neither; orcel-provider-uia resolves and validates the root (an element id it issued, of the same window, at the window's current tree generation, still bound to the same live window) before the window's element set is replaced, then observes below it with the existing depth, node and byte caps, redaction and protected-surface rules; the Windows native adapter and the computer host read below an element found by its runtime id inside the same live window, with the same bounds, and fail closed otherwise.

Slice 2, MCP: the local-only desktop_window_tree tool (SG-000063) gains the same two optional arguments; its contract, discovery, documentation and remote-scope tables change together; remote, tunnel and public profiles are unchanged.

Slice 3, qualification: BM-02 Tier C C2b on a disposable Windows CI runner reaches the cdb-s02 blocker form through a scoped subtree and its labelled scripted plan acts through the existing approval-gated set_value and invoke shapes with recorded broker decisions, evaluator scores and complete cleanup.
exclude: Any raise of MAX_TREE_DEPTH, MAX_TREE_NODES or the response byte bound.
Caller-supplied HWNDs, PIDs, runtime ids, native element handles, selectors, XPath or coordinates; UIA_WIDENING_FIELDS stays as it is.
Unrestricted traversal, standing enumeration or any observation that is not one bounded call over an Orcel-issued element.
New approval authority: every action keeps its fresh per-action SOFT approval; observation stays read-only.
Any change to actuation shapes, eligible control types, protected surfaces, other-session exclusion or the remote, tunnel and public profiles.
macOS and Linux native observation changes (outside this grain).

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000128; it adds no argument, shape, tool, dependency, listener or authority.
authority_delta.observation: Proposed only (slice 1): read-only bounded observation below an Orcel-issued element of the same window and current tree generation, under unchanged per-call caps, redaction and protected-surface rules.
authority_delta.mcp: Proposed only (slice 2): two optional arguments on the existing local-only desktop_window_tree tool; no new tool; remote, tunnel and public profiles unchanged.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules: no observation needs approval and every action on an observed element keeps its fresh per-action SOFT approval with exact digest binding, single use and expiry.
authority_delta.native_host: Proposed only (slice 1): one bounded host request (or field) reading below a runtime id inside the same live window; fails closed when the id does not resolve there.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

decisions.question: Open the governed change
decisions.decision: Founder decision of 2026-10-29, relayed by the implementing session and recorded on issue #515: "Approved: Open the governed change for Issue #515. I authorize the formal SpecGrain activation process and implementation of narrowly scoped UIA subtree observation, subject to all required governance, security reviews, and qualification gates. This authorization is limited to the scoped UIA capability described in PR #517. It does not authorize general UIA access, arbitrary element selectors, unrestricted tree traversal, or new approval authority."

decisions.question: Sequencing
decisions.decision: SG-000128 runs as an additional active grain beside SG-000096 and SG-000127; the canonical open-grain test records it.

decisions.question: Rule change: the lawful open-grain set
decisions.decision: The canonical open-grain rule (apps/orcel-mcp/src/openai-plugin.test.ts and p20-architecture.test.ts) allowed only SG-000096 with SG-000127. It now also allows SG-000096, SG-000127 and SG-000128 together, only while CURRENT.md records SG-000128's founder decision, the parallel grains SG-000108, SG-000120 and SG-000126 stay closed, and no other grain beyond SG-000096 exists. This follows the SG-000120 precedent (issue #455). No other rule changes.

decisions.question: Raise the global caps instead
decisions.decision: A larger global depth or node cap would enlarge every observation for every caller and widen SG-000063 A1's bound; a scoped root keeps every response within today's bound.

decisions.question: Known limitations (slice 1)
decisions.decision: A plan whose action is refused or fails cannot scope-read that window again until the window changes (fail closed). Budgets, element ids and window ids live in orceld's per-process registry, so an orceld restart resets them together with every identity (a restarted orceld has issued no roots). The Windows root search is bounded (4096 control-view nodes, depth 64): a root beyond it is refused as not found. If a final response exceeds the byte bound, the generation has already advanced and, for a scoped call, one budget slot is spent (fail closed, the existing response-bound pattern). Evidence split, recorded by the implementer: slice 1 proves the registry, policy and orceld refusal paths deterministically; orceld's scoped success path and the Windows native adapter (read_subtree, find_by_runtime_id) are evidenced live by slice 3 (BM-02 Tier C C2b on a disposable Windows CI runner); the computer host refuses scoped reads (ProviderUnavailable) until slice 1b adds its protocol request and tests.

decisions.question: Acceptance change: split slice 3 qualification into 3a (CI) and 3b (founder-present)
decisions.status: RECORDED (before implementation of 3a; independent review required)
decisions.decision: Run 40876732505 showed the scoped read reaching the form on the real application and the first set_value refused: "DesktopInput requires an active Orcel runtime session binding". DesktopInput needs a Full User lease, which only orcel-lifecycle's grant_full_user issues after a STRONG platform-presence approval. A CI runner has no person to give it, and granting the lease from a test (full_control_store::grant_local) would manufacture consent, which the founder directives forbid. Slice 3 is therefore split: 3a proves on CI everything that does not need a person (every target reached through the scoped read, the gate refusing the action, nothing written); 3b keeps the original end-to-end criterion unchanged and moves it to a founder-present run on a disposable machine. No gate, rule or bound is relaxed; the original slice 3 criterion is kept whole as 3b, and SG-000128 cannot close until 3b is accepted or the founder records a different decision.

decisions.question: Rule change: one more documented ignored test
decisions.decision: The release-blocker sweep (crates/orcel-lifecycle/tests/release_blocker_sweep.rs, only_the_documented_ignored_tests_exist) admits #[ignore] only at listed files with a listed reason. It now also admits crates/orceld/src/bm02_tier_c_act_tests.rs with the reason "run by the BM-02 Tier C harness (tierc-act) on a CI runner with the apps launched": a Windows test-build-only test (cfg(all(test, windows))) that the non-required Tier C GUI CI job runs for slice 3a and that slice 3b runs founder-present. It follows the existing per-file pattern; no other file or reason is admitted, and no other rule changes.

invariants: orceld remains the sole local authority; the MCP edge and clients only forward requests.
Every uia.tree observe response, scoped or not, stays within MAX_TREE_DEPTH (8 below its root), MAX_TREE_NODES (256) and the response byte bound.

A scoped root must be an element id orceld issued for the same window at that window's current tree generation and still bound to the same live window; anything else fails closed and observes nothing.
The root is resolved and validated before the window's element set is replaced.
Each observation, scoped or not, starts a new tree generation and replaces the window's elements: elements from an earlier observation are stale for actions.
The registry stays bounded: at most MAX_TREE_NODES elements per window and MAX_WINDOWS windows.
Redaction (password and secret-like values), protected-surface and other-session exclusions apply to every subtree.
No caller-supplied HWND, PID, runtime id, native handle, selector, XPath or coordinate is accepted.

Observation itself never asks for or creates approval; every action keeps its fresh per-action SOFT approval. The scoped budget is renewed only as a side effect of a real window change or a successful approved action; no new approval class exists.

Cumulative exposure is bounded by consent or a real window change: at most MAX_SCOPED_OBSERVATIONS (8) scoped observations per window between budget resets, and the budget resets only when the window's identity changes (process instance, nonce or class) or an approved action (fresh per-action SOFT approval) succeeds on that window. Listing an unchanged window and a title-only change (a web page's document.title, a ticking counter) do not reset it. Reading further than eight scoped responses into one window therefore needs a person's approval for an action in between or a real window change; unapproved traversal of an unchanged window stops at nine bounded responses (9 x 256 nodes).
acceptance: Policy tests: root_element_id and expected_tree_generation are accepted only together, are well formed, and every UIA_WIDENING_FIELDS field is still refused.

Provider tests: a stale generation, an element of another window, a malformed id, an unknown id, a root whose window was re-created, a root in a protected surface (or one that became protected) and a root that is gone or denied by UI Automation when read all fail closed and observe nothing; the root is validated before the element set is replaced; a scoped call starts a new generation and an action on an element from the previous call is refused as stale.
Bounds tests: a scoped subtree never exceeds depth 8 below its root, 256 nodes or the byte bound, and a password field inside it is redacted.

Cumulative-exposure tests: the ninth scoped observation of one unchanged window fails closed and observes nothing; listing the unchanged window again does not reset the budget; a changed window (new window generation) and a successful approved action on the window each reset it; a refused or failed action does not. The slice 1 security judge records an explicit cumulative-exposure analysis.
orceld tests: the scoped call through handle_envelope (profile gate, policy, dispatch, audit) observes below an issued root, every refusal is audited, and the unscoped call is unchanged.

Host protocol tests: the computer host request (or field) for a scoped read encodes exactly, is refused by a host that does not support it, and a runtime id that does not resolve inside the window fails closed.
Native tests on Windows: the host reads below a runtime id inside the same live window, refuses one that does not resolve there, and the live SG-000063 observation tests still pass.

MCP tests (slice 2): desktop_window_tree accepts the two optional arguments, the contract, discovery, documentation and remote-scope tables agree, and remote, tunnel and public profiles are unchanged.

Qualification (slice 3a, CI): BM-02 Tier C C2b on a disposable Windows CI runner, with the labelled scripted plan for cdb-s02's blocker form, reaches every plan element (the five fields and the button) through orceld's scoped subtree read on the real application, within the per-window budget; the first action is refused CAPABILITY_DENIED by the DesktopInput Full User gate; the evaluator shows no target check passed (nothing written); every call is audited and no window or process is left behind.

Qualification (slice 3b, founder-present): the same labelled scripted plan completes on a disposable Windows machine through the scoped subtree and the existing approval-gated actions, with the founder granting Full User through STRONG platform presence (Windows Hello), recorded broker decisions, evaluator scores showing the targets passed and the preserved checks intact, and no window or process left behind. Accepted by the founder; not run on the founder's live desktop.
Exact-head CI (Windows, macOS and Linux legs), Review Gates (Jev Semantic Review, Alibaba OpenCodeReview delegation) and a fresh-context security judge pass on each slice.

review.alibaba_open_code_review: delegation mode per standing founder decision (2026-10-10) with manual review of excluded files
review.security_review: fresh-context security judge on every slice and on closeout, with an explicit cumulative-exposure analysis on slice 1; d1-local advisory only

successor_requirements.macos_linux: Scoped subtree observation in the macOS and Linux native hosts is outside SG-000128.
successor_requirements.agent_runs: BM-02 Tier C agent runs (C3) still need a planner model decision.

activation_note: No argument, shape, tool, dependency or authority change in this activation packet. Separate implementation PRs must qualify their exact heads; activation CI alone proves nothing about subtree observation.
done_when: On Windows, uia.tree observe with a scoped root returns the bounded subtree below an Orcel-issued element under unchanged caps, redaction and protected-surface rules, every invalid root fails closed, desktop_window_tree exposes it locally with agreeing contract tables, and BM-02 Tier C C2b completes its labelled scripted plan through it on a disposable CI runner.
